name: Costa Rica La Minita Estate, Tarrazu
vendor_notes: Brilliant acidity, medium body, sweet orange citrus, caramelized sugar and fine chocolate; impeccably balanced with a long finish. Brightness 5/7, body 4/7, sweetness 5/7, balance 6/7. Grown 1,143-1,524 m. Rainforest Alliance.
goal: Light-medium roast: orange brightness over caramel and chocolate
rationale: A clean, well-sorted washed Caturra from Tarrazu (1,143-1,524 m): medium-high density that takes a normal charge (188 C) and develops evenly. Its appeal is balance, bright orange acidity over caramelized sugar and chocolate, so it sits between the light and medium plans: ~12 C after first crack, DTR ~20%. That keeps the orange while building the caramel and chocolate for espresso. FC 188 C follows the washed Central American coffees on this roaster.
steps: Preheat to 188 C, then hold steady 10+ min (BT/ET flat).
Charge 170 g at BT 188. Burner 72%, air 30, drum 90.
TP ~0:36 near 110 C. RoR is highest here, then falls.
At 178 C (~6:11): burner 46%. RoR ~10 and falling.
FC ~7:15 at ~188 C: burner 41%, air 55. Then 37%.
Drop ~9:05 at ~200 C (12 C after FC).

rest.note: Light-medium washed coffee: give it about a week. Orange and caramel are clearest from around day 9.

history.note: Initial light-to-medium plan from the Coffee Bean Corral page, using the measured opening on this roaster (TP ~0:36 at ~110 C) and FC 187-189 C from the Honduras and PNG roasts.
